dct_description_sm:
Family File

The Family file gives detailed information on the husband or male lone parent and the wife or female lone parent in the census family as well as grouped data on the other members of the family. A record, when dealing with the Family file, refers to data on one family unit. A census family consists of a husband and wife (with or without children who have nevered married, regardless of age) or a lone parent, regardless of marital status, with one or more children (who have never married, regardless of age) living in the same dwelling.

Individual File

The Individual File gives detailed demographic and economic data along with a few family and household characteristics for each individual in the sample. A record, when dealing with the Individual file, refers to data on one person.

Household File

The Household file contains detailed demographic information on the occupants of the household, as well as some information on housing. A record, when dealing with the Household file, refers to data on one household unit. A household refers to a person or group of persons (other than foreign residents) who occupy a dwelling and do not have usual place of residence elsewhere in Canada. It usually consists of a family group, with or without lodgers, employees, etc. However, it may consist of two or more families sharing a dwelling, a group of unrelated persons or one person living alone. Household members who are temporarily absent on Census Day (e.g., temporary residents elsewhere) are considered as part of their usual household for census purposes, every person is a member of one and only one household.
